science.title: Cometary tail detected on a near-Earth object based on nongravitational perturbations
science.description: Based on activity inferred from observed comet-like nongravitational acceleration, we report the detection of a cometary tail on a near-Earth object that was previously classified as inactive. This finding demonstrates that nongravitational accelerations can be used to infer the outgassing of ices on covertly ‘inactive’ objects such as dark comets.

science.title: Aligned graphite particles unlock stable levitation above magnets, study finds
science.description: A diamagnetic substance is slightly repelled by magnetic fields. With a strong enough magnet, the diamagnetic force can override gravity, and the substance will float in the air. Graphite, the main component of pencil lead, is considered one of the best substances for such real-world levitation, and its potential application in sensing weak external perturbations is drawing growing interest.

science.title: Astronomers catch a recurring black hole eruption in real time
science.description: For the third time in 35 years, the black hole at the center of the galaxy IC 3599 has erupted, and this time, astronomers were watching it closely. IC 3599, a galaxy roughly 280 million light-years away, has flared this dramatically twice before, in 1990 and 2010, but both eruptions were only pieced together after they had faded. This is the first time researchers have watched one of these outbursts unfold in real time. The paper outlining its multiwavelength analysis was posted to the arXiv preprint server on July 10.

ai.title: World shares mostly gain and South Korea and Japan recover some losses from AI stock sell-offs
ai.description: World shares have mostly gained and U.S. futures advanced, with markets in South Korea and Japan trading higher after recent declines due to heavy selling of stocks linked to artificial intelligence. South Korea's benchmark Kospi ended 3.6% higher led by technology shares, and Japan's Nikkei 225 jumped 3.3%. Oil prices are higher despite falling earlier in the day, taking Brent crude, the international standard, back to near $90 a barrel. That's well above the prewar level of about $72 a barrel. On Monday, Wall Street's benchmark S&P 500 slipped 0.2%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.6%, while the Nasdaq composite dipped less than 0.1%.
